### Given / unknowns and sign convention
Let pipe flow directions be:
- \(q_1:\) A→B, \(q_2:\) A→C, \(q_3:\) B→C, \(q_4:\) B→D, \(q_5:\) C→D, \(q_6:\) D→T.  
Withdrawal at B: \(Q_w=0.016\ \text{m}^3\!/\text{s}\).  
Pump flow \(Q_p = q_1+q_2\).

Continuity:
\[
\begin{aligned}
q_4 &= q_1-Q_w-q_3 \\
q_5 &= q_2+q_3 \\
q_6 &= q_4+q_5 = Q_p-Q_w
\end{aligned}
\]

Headloss in each pipe:
\[
h = \left(f\frac{L}{D}+\Sigma K\right)\frac{V^2}{2g}
= r\,Q|Q|,\qquad
r=\left(f\frac{L}{D}+\Sigma K\right)\frac{8}{\pi^2 g D^4}
\]

Pump curve (head added):
\[
H_p = 80 - 12000\,Q_p^2
\]
Suction pipe loss: \(h_s=r_s Q_p^2\).  
With tank S free surface head \(H_S=1\ \text{m}\), piezometric head at A is:
\[
H_A = H_S - h_s + H_p = 81 - (12000+r_s)Q_p^2
\]

Tank T free surface head \(H_T=14\ \text{m}\). Also \(H_D = H_T + h_6\).

---

## 1) Friction factors (Colebrook) and resistances \(r\) at the solution
Using Colebrook (via standard iteration) at 20 °C with the solved flows (found below), the Darcy factors are:

| Pipe | \(Q\) (m³/s) | Re (–) | \(f\) (–) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Suction | 0.04967 | \(3.14\times 10^5\) | 0.0164 |
| 1 | 0.03186 | \(3.21\times 10^5\) | 0.0244 |
| 2 | 0.01781 | \(2.26\times 10^5\) | 0.0185 |
| 3 | 0.00346 | \(5.73\times 10^4\) | 0.0265 |
| 4 | 0.01240 | \(1.56\times 10^5\) | 0.0263 |
| 5 | 0.02127 | \(2.15\times 10^5\) | 0.0180 |
| 6 | 0.03367 | \(2.83\times 10^5\) | 0.0171 |

Then \((fL/D+\Sigma K)\) and \(r\) become:

- Suction: \(fL/D=0.0164(30/0.2)=2.46\Rightarrow (\,)=3.86\Rightarrow r_s=199.3\)
- Pipe 1: \(fL/D=0.0244(300/0.125)=58.6\Rightarrow (\,)=62.6\Rightarrow r_1=21295\)
- Pipe 2: \(fL/D=0.0185(450/0.1)=83.3\Rightarrow (\,)=91.3\Rightarrow r_2=75400\)
- Pipe 3: \(fL/D=0.0265(200/0.075)=70.7\Rightarrow (\,)=73.7\Rightarrow r_3=192500\)
- Pipe 4: \(fL/D=0.0263(350/0.1)=92.1\Rightarrow (\,)=94.1\Rightarrow r_4=77750\)
- Pipe 5: \(fL/D=0.0180(400/0.125)=57.6\Rightarrow (\,)=62.6\Rightarrow r_5=21295\)
- Pipe 6: \(fL/D=0.0171(150/0.15)=17.1\Rightarrow (\,)=18.1\Rightarrow r_6=2954\)

(Units of all \(r\): \(\text{m}/(\text{m}^3/\text{s})^2\).)

---

## 2) Network equations (two loop/compatibility conditions)
From head relations between B, C, D:
\[
H_B-H_C = h_3 = r_3 q_3|q_3|
\]
but also
\[
H_B = H_D + r_4 q_4|q_4|,\quad
H_C = H_D + r_5 q_5|q_5|
\]
so
\[
r_4 q_4|q_4| - r_5 q_5|q_5| = r_3 q_3|q_3|\tag{E1}
\]

From A→B and A→C consistency:
\[
H_A = H_B + r_1 q_1|q_1| = H_C + r_2 q_2|q_2|
\]
\[
(H_B-H_C)+r_1 q_1|q_1| - r_2 q_2|q_2|=0
\]
Using \(H_B-H_C=r_3 q_3|q_3|\):
\[
r_3 q_3|q_3| + r_1 q_1|q_1| - r_2 q_2|q_2|=0\tag{E2}
\]

Pump/system head equation using path A→B→D→T:
\[
H_A = 14 + r_6 q_6^2 + r_4 q_4^2 + r_1 q_1^2\tag{E3a}
\]
and pump gives
\[
H_A = 81-(12000+r_s)Q_p^2,\quad Q_p=q_1+q_2\tag{E3b}
\]
Solve (E1)(E2)(E3a=E3b) with the continuity substitutions.

---

## 3) Solved flows
Solving the above nonlinear system (with \(f\) updated by Colebrook to match each pipe’s Reynolds number) gives:

\[
\boxed{Q_p = 0.04967\ \text{m}^3/\text{s}}
\]
and internal flows:
\[
q_1=0.03186,\;
q_2=0.01781,\;
q_3=0.00346,\;
q_4=0.01240,\;
q_5=0.02127,\;
q_6=0.03367
\quad (\text{m}^3/\text{s})
\]
(\(q_3>0\) so flow is B→C.)

---

## (b) Pump head added
\[
H_p = 80-12000Q_p^2
=80-12000(0.04967)^2
=80-29.61=50.40\ \text{m}
\]

---

## (d) Gauge pressure at node C
First compute heads from T back to C:
\[
h_6=r_6 q_6^2 = 2954(0.03367)^2 = 3.35\ \text{m}
\]
\[
H_D = H_T + h_6 = 14 + 3.35 = 17.35\ \text{m}
\]
\[
h_5=r_5 q_5^2 = 21295(0.02127)^2 = 9.64\ \text{m}
\]
\[
H_C = H_D + h_5 = 17.35+9.64=26.99\ \text{m}
\]
Gauge pressure:
\[
p_C = \rho g (H_C-z_C)
=998.2(9.81)(26.99-4.00)
=2.249\times 10^5\ \text{Pa}
=224.9\ \text{kPa}
\]

---

## (e) Pump shaft power
Hydraulic power:
\[
P_h=\rho g Q_p H_p
=998.2(9.81)(0.04967)(50.40)=24.50\ \text{kW}
\]
With \(\eta=0.70\):
\[
P_{\text{shaft}}=\frac{P_h}{\eta}=\frac{24.50}{0.70}=35.0\ \text{kW}
\]

---

FINAL (a): 49.7 L/s  
FINAL (b): 50.4 m  
FINAL (c): 3.46 L/s (from B to C)  
FINAL (d): 225 kPa  
FINAL (e): 35.0 kW
